title: WooCommerce Shipping and Fulfillment: Setup, Your Options, and How ShipBob Plugs In
summary: Here's what you need to know about shipping for your WooCommerce store, including shipping setup, fulfillment options and how ShipBob fits in.
body_markdown:
[WooCommerce](https://woocommerce.com/) has grown from a simple WordPress plugin to a fully customizable ecommerce platform. It gives your store near-total control over how you sell. But that flexibility means WooCommerce fulfillment is something each brand designs, not something the platform handles for you.


As your store grows, fulfillment stops being a plugin decision and becomes an operating-model decision. It determines your shipping speed, your costs, and the experience every customer has after they check out.


This guide covers what WooCommerce fulfillment includes, your main options, and a condensed setup walkthrough. We also cover when to move to a[fulfillment partner](https://www.shipbob.com/ecommerce-fulfillment/) , and how ShipBob connects to your store.


## What WooCommerce fulfillment actually covers


On the backend of your store, WooCommerce makes it easy to calculate shipping rates based on zones and product weights. It also gives you tools to group products and apply different shipping methods to each group.


Order fulfillment is everything that happens after that: receiving inventory, picking, packing, shipping, tracking, customer notifications, returns, and order status updates.


For that path to work, data has to move between systems. Order details, tracking numbers, carrier info, and delivery updates flow between WooCommerce and whatever tools handle each step of the[order fulfillment process](https://www.shipbob.com/blog/order-fulfillment/) .


Some of that flow is customer-facing. For example, automated tracking emails, delivery notifications, and WooCommerce order status changes keep shoppers informed from “processing” to “delivered.” But as volume grows, fulfillment gets more complex, and you start dealing with partial fulfillment, split shipments, multi-package orders, and orders that ship from different locations.


WooCommerce added a native Order Fulfillments feature that supports per-item tracking to help. It works alongside plugins and third-party providers rather than replacing them.


## Your WooCommerce fulfillment options, from plugins to a fulfillment partner


Depending on business size, order volume, location, and a variety of other factors, different ecommerce businesses have different needs. The best WooCommerce fulfillment option for your business might be different from that of your competitors.


Below are the main ways WooCommerce brands get orders out the door, sequenced from lowest-lift to fully outsourced. Most brands move through several of them as volume grows.


### Native WooCommerce order management


On its own, WooCommerce handles the basics of order management. It tracks order statuses, supports manual updates, and includes a native Order Fulfillments feature with per-item tracking.


A couple of official extensions add more functionality. WooCommerce Shipping is now a separate labels extension that prints USPS, UPS, and DHL Express labels, with FedEx being added. Plus, WooCommerce Tax handles sales tax separately.


These native tools track orders and print labels, but that’s the ceiling. They don’t pick, pack, or store your inventory, so the physical work still falls on you.


### Shipping and fulfillment plugins and extensions


Plugins, extensions, and APIs are the standard way WooCommerce brands automate fulfillment workflows. They connect your store to the tools that do the work behind each order.


A plugin might add rate calculation at checkout, label printing, tracking sync, or a direct carrier connection. You mix and match them to fit how your store ships.


There are far too many to cover here, and new ones launch often. For a fuller look, see our round-up of[shipping and fulfillment plugins](https://www.shipbob.com/shipping-fulfillment-plugins/) .


### Shipping software and carrier tools


Shipping software sits between WooCommerce and your carriers. Tools like ShipStation and carrier dashboards centralize label buying and let you ship with multiple carriers from one screen.


This works well for brands still holding their own inventory. The software finds rates and prints labels, but you still store products, pick, pack, and manage the day-to-day yourself.


In other words, it speeds up the admin without removing it. As order volume climbs, that manual work grows right along with it.


### In-house fulfillment and WMS software


Also called merchant fulfillment or self-fulfillment, in-house fulfillment means you complete the entire order fulfillment process for your WooCommerce store yourself. That runs from storing[ecommerce inventory](https://www.shipbob.com/ecommerce-inventory/guide/) to shipping orders, without the help of a third party.


Many WooCommerce store owners choose to[fulfill orders in-house](https://www.shipbob.com/blog/self-fulfillment/) when they first start out, often storing inventory and packing orders from home. You can use any of the WooCommerce shipping settings we mentioned earlier.


As you grow, many brands run a warehouse management system (WMS) to stay organized. A WMS adds inventory accuracy checks, structured pick and pack workflows, and location-level visibility into your stock.


In-house[retail fulfillment](https://www.shipbob.com/blog/retail-fulfillment/) can be expensive and time-consuming to scale. It fits best at low volume, or when you sell custom or specialized products that need hands-on handling. It tends to strain under multi-region shipping, peak-season spikes, and the headcount required to keep up.


### Dropshipping


If you’d rather take an “out of sight, out of mind” approach to order fulfillment, dropshipping may be a better choice. The order details are forwarded to the manufacturer, and the product ships directly from the manufacturer to the end consumer.


Dropshipping requires minimal overhead and removes the need to store inventory yourself. But it offers little to no control over your[ecommerce supply chain](https://www.shipbob.com/blog/ecommerce-supply-chain/) . Many suppliers are also overseas, so shipping can take longer and cost more than fulfilling orders domestically.


### Outsourced fulfillment and 3PL partners


Third-party logistics refers to outsourcing WooCommerce logistics, including inventory management and the picking, packing, and shipping of orders. A WooCommerce[3PL](https://www.shipbob.com/blog/3pls-from-a-to-z-definitions-for-e-commerce-order-fulfillment/) , or fulfillment partner, takes over storage, picking, packing, shipping, and returns so you stop managing warehouse operations directly.


A fulfillment-partner integration automates order syncing, inventory updates, tracking, and returns between your store and the partner’s systems. That’s where WooCommerce fulfillment services move from a settings task to a hands-off operation.


This is the option most brands move toward once fulfillment becomes an operating-model decision rather than a plugin choice. Providers like these are 3PL’s though ShipBob functions more like a fulfillment partner than a traditional 3PL.

## How to set up shipping in WooCommerce


To complete your WooCommerce shipping setup, you create shipping zones, followed by shipping methods and rates.


### Shipping zones, classes, and rates


A WooCommerce[shipping zone](https://www.shipbob.com/ecommerce-shipping/shipping-zones/) is a geographical area where certain shipping methods and rates apply, and each customer address maps to only one zone. To set one up, go to WooCommerce > Settings > Shipping, add a zone with a name and region, then assign shipping methods to it.


Shipping classes let you group products that ship differently by size or weight and charge each group its own rate. Common rate methods include[flat-rate shipping](https://www.shipbob.com/blog/flat-rate-shipping/) , free shipping, and real-time carrier rates. Flat rate fits predictable costs, free shipping helps lift conversion, and real-time rates matter most when accuracy does.


For label printing, use the current WooCommerce Shipping extension, which prints USPS, UPS, and DHL Express labels, with FedEx being added. For the full step-by-step, see the[official WooCommerce documentation](https://woocommerce.com/document/setting-up-shipping-zones/) .


### Showing real-time and 2-day rates at checkout


You can show estimated real-time rates at checkout so shoppers pay closer to the true cost of fulfilling their order. That accuracy helps boost conversions because surprise shipping costs are on of the[top reasons carts get abandoned](https://baymard.com/lists/cart-abandonment-rate) .


Our ShipBob Express Rates plugin is how ShipBob merchants surface those estimated real-time rates in WooCommerce. You install it from WordPress, and it also enables WooCommerce Real-Time Rates.


If you want to offer 2-day delivery, ShipBob’s 2-Day Express option covers 100% of the contiguous US, even from a single fulfillment center. It’s configured separately on ShipBob’s side and enabled in WooCommerce through the plugin. See how to set up[2-Day Express shipping](https://support.shipbob.com/s/article/WooCommerce-2-day-setup) for the steps.


## When to move from plugins or in-house to a WooCommerce fulfillment partner


Most WooCommerce brands don’t pick one fulfillment method and stop. They tend to move through stages as they grow:


1. Manual and native tools
2. Plugins
3. Shipping software
4. WMS
5. Outsourced partner


Many settle on a hybrid of the last two.


There are a few signals tell you you’ve outgrown manual and plugin workflows, but the hard part is scaling past those workflows without simply hiring more people. Hands-off automation is how brands add volume without adding headcount, because the software and the partner absorb the extra work.


Use this quick checklist to see where you stand:


- Order volume: how many orders you ship each day, and how fast that number is rising.
- Order complexity: bundles, kits, split shipments, and multi-package orders.
- Number of channels: how many stores, marketplaces, and B2B accounts you sell through.
- Shipping-speed goals: whether you want to offer 2-day or next-day delivery.
- Available team time: how many hours go to manual order administration each week.


For high-volume DTC and omnichannel brands, this is an operating-model decision.

## WooCommerce fulfillment FAQs


#### Does ShipBob integrate directly with WooCommerce?


Yes. You connect your store from the ShipBob dashboard by approving access in WooCommerce, and there’s nothing to install for the core integration.


#### How do orders and tracking flow between WooCommerce and ShipBob?


Orders in “Processing” status import to ShipBob automatically every 30 minutes, and you can bring in up to 120 days of history at setup. Once an order ships, tracking posts back through the WooCommerce Shipment Tracking extension, or into your order notes if you don’t use it.


#### What is the difference between a WooCommerce fulfillment plugin and a fulfillment partner?


A plugin adds a single capability, like rate calculation, label printing, or tracking sync, but you still store, pick, pack, and ship every order. A fulfillment partner takes over the physical operation and automates your order, inventory, and tracking sync.


#### Does ShipBob work alongside my other sales channels and marketplaces?


Yes. ShipBob supports DTC, B2B, and marketplace orders from one shared inventory pool, so your WooCommerce store runs alongside your other channels in a single dashboard.


#### What shipping costs can WooCommerce merchants expect from ShipBob?


ShipBob rate-shops across carriers on every package and negotiates bulk discounts, so each brand gets a custom quote. Our Inventory Placement Program also distributes inventory closer to customers to cut zones and costs.


Pricing is all-in, combining the label, picks, packaging, and labor into one fee. See[fulfillment pricing](https://www.shipbob.com/pricing/) for details.


#### Do I need to install anything to connect WooCommerce to ShipBob?


No separate app is required for the core integration. You connect your store from the ShipBob dashboard by approving access in WooCommerce.


Tracking write-back uses the WooCommerce Shipment Tracking extension, and estimated checkout rates use the ShipBob Express Rates plugin. Even so, the core order and fulfillment sync doesn’t need additional installations.
